current_example.title: Example: Applying the Laplace Transform to a System of Linear ODEs

q-332820.name: Question 1
q-332820.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)+6 \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-3{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t)+1,\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation, we get the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)={{field-1}} \\ {{field-2}}=-3{X}_{1}(s)+2{X}_{2}(s)+{{field-3}}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}$ are the Laplace transforms of the functions ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t),$ respectively.
q-332820.worked_solution:
First, we compute the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{{x}_{1}(t)+6\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{-3{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t)+1\}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+6L\{1\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=-3L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+2L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}+L\{1\}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the result

$$
L\{1\}=\frac{1}{s},
$$

 we can write our system as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)={X}_{1}(s)+\frac{6}{s} \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-1=-3{X}_{1}(s)+2{X}_{2}(s)+\frac{1}{s}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}$ are the Laplace transforms of the functions ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t),$ respectively.

First, we compute the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{2{x}_{1}(t)+2{e}^{-t}\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t)+3\}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=2L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+2L\{{e}^{-t}\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}+3L\{1\}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the results

$$
L\{1\}=\frac{1}{s},\,L\{{e}^{-t}\}=\frac{1}{s+1},
$$

we can write our system as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)=2{X}_{1}(s)+\frac{2}{s+1} \\ s{X}_{2}(s)+1={X}_{1}(s)+{X}_{2}(s)+\frac{3}{s}\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}$ are the Laplace transforms of the functions ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t),$ respectively.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{{x}_{1}(t)+5{e}^{3t}\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{-2{x}_{1}(t)+4{x}_{2}(t)-1\}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+5L\{{e}^{3t}\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=-2L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+4L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-L\{1\}\end{aligned}
$$

L\{1\}=\frac{1}{s},\,L\{{e}^{3t}\}=\frac{1}{s-3},

$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}$ are the Laplace transforms of the functions ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t),$ respectively.
